chapterNote: The shortest and strangest of the Zion songs, and the one with the widest door. The LORD loves the gates of Zion above every other dwelling of Jacob; glorious things are spoken of the city of God — John Newton's hymn and Augustine's title both come from that line. Then God speaks, and what He says is a birth-register: Rahab, which is Egypt, and Babylon, the two great oppressors; Philistia, Tyre, and Cush — 'this one was born there.' Of Zion it will be said, this one and that one were born in her, and the LORD Himself keeps the ledger as He writes up the peoples. The enemies' natives are counted as Zion's children: a city with more sons on its rolls than people in its streets, the Jerusalem above that Paul calls the mother of us all. The last line is sung by the musicians: all my springs are in you. Every fountain the nations drink from rises there.

1.text: A psalm of the sons of Korah, a song. What He has founded stands on the holy mountains.
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] or Song [shir] for the sons [ben] of Korah. His foundation is in the holy [qodesh] mountains.
1.notes: yesudato be-harere-qodesh (H6944): 'His foundation' — the city's, or God's own founding — on the holy mountains; the psalm opens mid-thought, as if the singer were already looking at Jerusalem's hills (cf. Psalm 125:2). Korah's sons, the temple singers, wrote most of the Psalter's Zion songs (42-49, 84-88).

2.text: The LORD loves Zion's gates above all the dwelling places of Jacob.
2.amp: The LORD [YHWH] loves [ahab] the gates [shaar] of Zion [Tsiyyon] more than all the dwellings [mishkan] of Jacob [Yaaqob].
2.notes: oheb YHWH shaare Tsiyyon mi-kol mishkenot Yaaqob (H157, H3068, H8179, H6726, H4908, H3290): the LORD LOVES Zion's gates more than every other dwelling of Jacob — a chosen city inside a chosen people, Deuteronomy 12:5's 'place which the LORD shall choose'. Gates, because a city is known by who is let in — which is the psalm's subject.

3.text: Glorious things are being spoken of you, O city of God. Selah.
3.amp: Glorious things [kabad — weighty things] are spoken [dabar] of you, O city [ir] of God [Elohim]. Selah [Selah].
3.notes: nikhbadot medubbar bakh ir ha-Elohim (H3513, H1696, H5892, H430): glorious things — nikhbadot, weighty things — are being spoken IN you, or of you, city of God. John Newton's hymn 'Glorious things of thee are spoken' is this verse; Augustine took the title of his great book from the psalm's phrase, the city of God. Selah: pause before the glorious things are actually listed.

4.text: 'I will count Rahab and Babylon among those who know Me; look — Philistia and Tyre, with Cush: this one was born there.'
4.amp: I will make mention [zakar — record] of Rahab and Babylon [Babel] to them that know [yada] Me: behold Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia; this man was born [yalad] there.
4.notes: azkir Rahab u-Babel le-yodeai (H2142, H894, H3045): I will RECORD Rahab — the sea-monster nickname for Egypt (Isaiah 30:7) — and Babylon among those who know Me: the two great oppressors, enrolled; hinneh Pheleshet ve-Tsor im-Kush: look, Philistia, Tyre, Cush — zeh yullad-sham (H3205): 'this one was born there' — in Zion. God speaking, taking a census in which the enemies' natives are registered as Zion's children: Isaiah 19:24-25's 'Egypt my people' in a psalm, and Galatians 4:26's Jerusalem above, the mother of us all, behind it.

5.text: And of Zion it will be said, 'This one and that one were born in her' — and the Most High Himself will make her firm.
5.amp: And of Zion [Tsiyyon] it shall be said [amar], This and that man [ish] was born [yalad] in her: and the highest [Elyon] Himself shall establish [kun] her.
5.notes: u-le-Tsiyyon yeamar ish ve-ish yullad-bah (H6726, H559, H376, H3205): and of Zion it will be said, 'man and man' — this one and that one — 'was born in her': a city whose birth-register is longer than its population; ve-hu yekhoneneha Elyon (H3559, H5945): and He, the Most High, makes her firm. Psalm 48:8's 'God makes her stand firm', with the reason: she is a mother.

6.text: The LORD will count as He writes up the peoples: 'This one was born there.' Selah.
6.amp: The LORD [YHWH] shall count [saphar], when He writes up [kathab — registers] the people [am], that this man was born [yalad] there. Selah [Selah].
6.notes: YHWH yispor bi-khtob ammim zeh yullad-sham (H3068, H5608, H3789, H5971, H3205): the LORD COUNTS as He REGISTERS the peoples — the census-scroll of Psalm 69:28 and Malachi 3:16, with a birthplace column — 'this one was born there'. The third time the line is sung. Citizenship by new birth, entered by God's own hand (cf. John 3:3; Philippians 3:20; Revelation 21:27).

7.text: Singers and dancers alike will say, 'All my springs are in you.'
7.amp: As well the singers [shir] as the players on instruments [chalal — pipers, dancers] shall be there: all my springs [maayan] are in you.
7.notes: ve-sharim ke-cholelim (H7891, H2490): singers like pipers — or dancers; the word is the flute-players' — kol-mayanai bakh (H4599): 'all my springs are in you'. The last line of the psalm and its whole point: every fountain the nations drink from rises in Zion — Ezekiel 47:1's river from under the threshold, John 7:38's rivers of living water. The city of God is the world's waterworks.
